Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a smaller piece of the same problem. Each recursive call works on a reduced version of the input, and the process continues until it reaches a simple case that can be solved directly—called the base case. After the base case returns a result, each earlier call “unwinds,” using that result to build up the final answer. Think of it like a set of nested Russian dolls: you open one doll (make a recursive call) until you reach the smallest doll (the base case), then you put the dolls back together in reverse order.
